prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Conroe, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1458; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Can you confirm you're okay to proceed and that you understand this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, that's fine. I understand it's being recorded.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection in Conroe?

A: I was driving through the intersection on a green light. I had the right of way heading straight. Another vehicle came from the cross street and pulled out in front of me, and we collided on the driver's side of my car.

Q: Was your vehicle moving at the time of impact, and about how fast were you going?

A: Yes, I was moving at a normal speed, probably around the posted limit. I'd say maybe thirty-five or so. I was just starting to cross when the other car hit me.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact, or did it come in suddenly?

A: It came in pretty suddenly. I glimpsed it at the last second, and I tried to brake, but there wasn't enough time.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did the airbags deploy in your vehicle?

A: The side curtain airbag came out, I think. The front ones didn't.

Q: Have you been seen by a medical provider since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the same day. They diagnosed me with neck and back strain. I've been doing some physical therapy and I'm still having stiffness and soreness.

Q: Has anything else come up, such as headaches, numbness, or pain in other areas?

A: Mostly it's my neck and lower back. I get some tightness in my shoulders too, but no numbness or tingling that I've noticed.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get this resolved and get back to normal.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the recorded statement.

A: Thanks.
